clue.text: Search shed, in which Cameron finally is found?

indicators.note: in which ... is found says the next piece sits inside the shed word

parts.note: a garden shed is a hut

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of Cameron

explanation.surface: A search of a shed turns up the former Prime Minister David Cameron hiding inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Hunt, a Conservative minister, is one of many government members in this grid; Cameron is just the source of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunt for something is to search for it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Theresa — in a mopy huff — flipped over a tendency for reckless spending

indicators.note: flipped says the hidden letters are turned round and read backwards
over here means spanning, the run of letters stretching over several of the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Theresa May, sulking, flips over, as if her mood swing drives a spending spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped over' does double duty: 'over' marks a run of letters spanning the words, 'flipped' reads it backwards. The dash is punctuation only.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypomania is a mild form of mania whose classic symptoms include impulsive, reckless spending sprees.

clue.text: Untie puppy, frequently having a tendency to bite

indicators.note: frequently says take every other letter, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Advice not to unleash a puppy that keeps snapping at people.
explanation.definitionFit: A nippy dog is one inclined to nip, that is to give small bites.

clue.text: Summary of key points?

parts.note: the ... summarises the day's main stories, and also lists the four compass points north, east, west and south by their initials

explanation.walkthrough: The key points here are the cardinal points of the compass, whose initial letters in order make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A news bulletin gives the main points of the day, and the word is also the four compass initials.

clue.text: Blunder about French coast being an environmental threat

indicators.note: about says the blunder word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a blunder is an error
côte is the French word for coast

explanation.surface: A mistake on the French coastline turns out to be a danger to the environment, like an oil spill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French coast' wants to be a place in the surface; it is simply the French word côte, without its accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eco-terror is violence or sabotage in the name of environmental causes, or a threat to the environment itself.

clue.text: Henry — your Majesty — touring the county

indicators.note: touring says the royal address goes round the next letter

parts.note: sire is the old form of address to a king
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: King Henry tours his county with a royal party.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like the king being addressed, but it supplies only the H of the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shire is an English county; 'the Shires' are the rural counties.

clue.text: Painful condition keeping radius in plaster

indicators.note: keeping says the condition holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

explanation.surface: A painful injury to the radius bone means the arm is in a plaster cast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a broken arm in plaster; radius is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: Grout is a thin plaster or mortar used to fill gaps between tiles.

clue.text: Daughter leaves niggardly, hopeless ferryman

indicators.note: hopeless says the remaining letters are in a hopeless jumble

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter walks out on her mean, useless ferryman of a father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daughter leaves' takes D out of NIGGARDLY; 'hopeless' shuffles the remaining NIGGARLY. Chris Grayling, Transport Secretary, notoriously awarded a Brexit ferry contract to a firm with no ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Grayling earned the nickname through a no-deal ferry contract with a company that owned no ferries.

clue.text: Begin to give a speech about independent spirit

indicators.note: about says the speech word wraps round the following pieces

parts.note: to orate is to give a speech
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A speech about the spirit of independence is how a movement begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'independent spirit' reads as one idea but splits into I and GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or arise, a direct synonym.

clue.text: "Support Turkey!" — American Senate's leader

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
US means American

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rallying cry backing Turkey, issued by the head of the American Senate.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss, then a cabinet minister, is part of the theme of Conservative politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a supporting framework or a surgical support, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Katy's conference tipple?

definitions.meaning: Katy ... is the American pop singer, so this is Katy's surname
Conference is a popular British pear variety, and the drink fermented from pears is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: Conference pears are a common British variety; the lower-case 'conference' hides the proper name, and the political conference is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry is cider made from pears, and also the singer's surname.

clue.text: Coach for city with beer and sausage

parts.note: Pep Guardiola is the manager of Manchester City football club
Peroni is an Italian beer brand

explanation.surface: A football coach treats his club to beer and sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-American salami, a kind of sausage.

clue.text: Goodbye, moving 18 27 soon?

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: 18 is the answer to that clue, meaning help for a disaster
the European Union would have 27 members after Britain left

explanation.surface: A farewell as Britain moves away from the EU's 27 other members, which may happen soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shuffles AID with EU. The question mark hints the departure was still uncertain.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a borrowed French word for farewell.

clue.text: Right infiltrates PM's support — it has many branches

parts.note: Theresa May was Prime Minister at the time

indicators.note: infiltrates says the letter gets inside the other pieces

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Right-wingers sneak into the Prime Minister's support base, a party with many factions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM's' means Theresa May, the Prime Minister when the puzzle appeared; 'support' is the golfer's tee.
explanation.definitionFit: The may tree, or hawthorn, is a tree, and trees have many branches.

clue.text: 9's resolved to start with English pastries

indicators.note: resolved to start with says one letter is shifted so that it opens the word

parts.note: 9 is the surname of Claire Perry, a Conservative minister, so this means the possessive of her first name

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to begin with English pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: An indirect step: the 9 entry suggests Claire Perry, whose possessive first name has its E (for English) moved to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are long choux pastries filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Off games? Absolutely not!

parts.note: a thing that is off is no go, so off gives no
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: A pupil asks if games are cancelled and gets a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nope is a casual, emphatic form of no, a flat refusal.

clue.text: Rampant GI shot flier

indicators.note: shot says the letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier running amok shoots down a bird or a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: Flier suggests an airman; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions, and as a bird it is a flier.

clue.text: Brother Livingstone is finished

parts.note: Ken Livingstone is the former Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A political verdict that Ken Livingstone's career is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone is a British left-wing politician, former Mayor of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken is done for or finished, like a broken man.

clue.text: Abducted Nad, drunk, having slept around

indicators.note: around says the sleep word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: kip is British slang for sleep, so kipped means slept

indicators.note: drunk says the letters stagger into another order

explanation.surface: A man named Nad, drunk and having slept around, gets snatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' shuffles the three letters of the name; 'around' is not sleeping around but the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to abduct them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: I'm plugging commercial for disaster relief

indicators.note: plugging means filling a hole, so the letter goes into the middle

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
read as I am, so the letter I is doing the plugging

explanation.surface: A celebrity promoting a commercial for a disaster relief appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' looks like advertising, but it means filling a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid is help sent to a stricken area, such as relief after a disaster.

clue.text: It's naturally sweet to see a Lord on telly

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to date them
Lord Sugar, Alan Sugar, is the boss on the TV show The Apprentice

explanation.surface: A fan wants to see a peer who appears on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Date sugar is ground dried dates, a natural sweetener.

clue.text: Sports car ferrying upper-class Duncan Smith at the front takes the breath away

indicators.note: ferrying says the car carries the next letter inside it

parts.note: an Aston (Martin) is a sports car

indicators.note: at the front picks the opening letter of each name

explanation.surface: Iain Duncan Smith being driven in a sports car is breathtaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Iain Duncan Smith is a Conservative former party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that astounds amazes you, leaving you breathless.

clue.text: The range of Chagall

indicators.note: of says the letters are taken from within the painter's name

explanation.surface: Discussing the breadth of Marc Chagall's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Range reads as scope; it is a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aga is a large British cast-iron cooking range.

clue.text: Activates Trident, picking up the pace?

indicators.note: picking up says the letters are collected from inside the phrase

explanation.surface: The Trident nuclear deterrent is switched on as tension speeds up.
explanation.walkthrough: Mel Stride is a Conservative minister in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step, a single pace.

clue.text: Examine competition (ignoring Tories)

indicators.note: ignoring says the following piece is left out

parts.note: a contest is a competition
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Assessing a leadership contest without the Conservative party involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to examine it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Constable wishes to hug Inspector

indicators.note: to hug says the outer letters embrace the run inside them

explanation.surface: A police constable wants to embrace his inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Lewis is a British TV detective, sidekick to Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Lewis is a well-known British television police detective.

clue.text: Ah! Mr Goodman, playing new instrument

indicators.note: playing says the letters are played around with

explanation.surface: Someone sighs as Mr Goodman tries out a new musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip Hammond was Chancellor of the Exchequer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hammond organ is a well-known electric organ, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Leaders of Home Office order cheap home-made booze

indicators.note: leaders of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Home Office chiefs order a cheap home-brewed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang for cheap, illicit or home-made alcohol.

clue.text: Medic suppressing anger…it's got even worse

indicators.note: suppressing says the doctor holds the next word down inside

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A doctor bottles up his rage, and things get worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful, so the comparative is more dreadful still.

clue.text: Pies cooked on board a ship where no germs are present

indicators.note: on board says the next piece is inside the ship

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: cooked says the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Pies are baked aboard ship in a very clean galley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' reorders the letters of Pies, and the result goes on board, inside the steamship letters after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Asepsis is the state of being free of disease-causing microorganisms.

clue.text: Disgraced Liberal Farron put up in small hotel

indicators.note: in says the reversed name is placed inside the small hotel letters

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: put up in a down clue says the name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Tim Farron is a former Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: Tim Farron is housed in a little hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyril Smith was a Liberal MP later exposed as a child abuser. 'Liberal Farron' looks like one name, but Liberal belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Cyril Smith was a Liberal MP disgraced after his death by abuse revelations.

clue.text: See 25
Fixing Republican broadcast

parts.note: airing a programme is broadcasting it

explanation.surface: A Republican broadcast is rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: Fixing hints at rigging; it means mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairing something is fixing it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: German chap importing Dutch bananas

indicators.note: importing says the next letter is brought inside

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German man imports Dutch bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: Greg Hands is a Conservative minister in the theme. Bananas could be mad; it is fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas grow and are sold in bunches called hands, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Amber fish …

definitions.meaning: Amber ... was a Conservative Home Secretary, so this is Amber's surname
a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.definitionFit: Rudd is both the surname of the politician and the name of a reddish freshwater fish.

clue.text: … caught by that lady who was in Mermaids

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
her refers to that lady

explanation.surface: Continuing the fish theme: an amber fish caught by a woman who played a mermaid.
explanation.walkthrough: Mermaids is a 1990 film starring the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cher starred alongside Winona Ryder in the 1990 film Mermaids.
